diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, NOS, non-germinal-center (non-GCB) phenotype by the Hans algorithm (CD10-, BCL6+, MUM1+). Hans is an immunohistochemical surrogate and is not equivalent to molecular ABC cell-of-origin by gene-expression profiling. EBER negative; CD5 negative. The left axillary node is lymphoma, not recurrent breast carcinoma: cytokeratin AE1/AE3 and GATA3 are negative and there is no epithelial component.
stage: Lugano (Ann Arbor) stage IV with B symptoms (fevers to 38.4 C and night sweats): the multiple FDG-avid splenic nodules are extranodal organ involvement, in addition to nodes on both sides of the diaphragm. Largest mass 7.5 cm, below the 10 cm bulk threshold.
biology: Double-expressor lymphoma by IHC (MYC 45%, at or above the 40% threshold; BCL2 70%, above the 50% threshold), which carries a somewhat worse prognosis with standard immunochemotherapy. Not double-hit: FISH shows no MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement, so this is not high-grade B-cell lymphoma. Double-expressor status alone does not justify DA-EPOCH-R or other intensified regimens. Ki-67 ~80%.
prognosis: IPI 3 of 5 (high-intermediate risk): LDH elevated, stage IV and one extranodal site (spleen). CNS-IPI 3 of 6 (intermediate risk).
first_line_treatment: Curative intent. The key issue is cardiac: she received cumulative doxorubicin 240 mg/m2 (dose-dense AC-T, 2016) plus left breast radiotherapy, and LVEF has fallen from 62% (2016) to 45% with GLS -14% and mild global hypokinesis, a >10-point decline to <50% consistent with cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (asymptomatic, NYHA I). Standard full-dose doxorubicin (R-CHOP or Pola-R-CHP) should not be given in this setting. Urgent cardio-oncology referral before cycle 1, with guideline-directed cardioprotection: start an ACE inhibitor or ARB (e.g. switch amlodipine to lisinopril or candesartan) plus a beta-blocker (carvedilol), titrated as blood pressure allows. Recommend curative-intent R-CEOP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, etoposide, vincristine, prednisone; etoposide substituted for doxorubicin) for 6 cycles as an anthracycline-free regimen; R-GCVP (gemcitabine in place of doxorubicin) is an alternative. Tell the patient that anthracycline-free regimens likely have lower efficacy (cure rates) than anthracycline-based therapy, based on retrospective data. An anthracycline-modified option (R-CHOP with liposomal doxorubicin or with dexrazoxane) is acceptable only if cardio-oncology judges the cardiac risk acceptable after evaluation and optimization. Monitor during therapy with serial echocardiography (LVEF and GLS) every 2-3 cycles and at end of treatment, plus high-sensitivity troponin and NT-proBNP at baseline and with each cycle. DA-EPOCH-R is not indicated: double-expressor status alone does not justify intensification, and it also contains doxorubicin.
cns_risk: Intermediate CNS-relapse risk (CNS-IPI 2). No high-risk anatomic sites: no kidney, adrenal, testicular or breast involvement (the axillary node is lymphoma and the breasts show no uptake), and she has no neurological symptoms. No routine CNS prophylaxis is recommended (no high-dose methotrexate, no intrathecal therapy). MRI brain and lumbar puncture only if neurological symptoms develop.
response_assessment: End-of-treatment FDG PET-CT 6-8 weeks after the last cycle, read with Lugano 2014 criteria and the Deauville 5-point scale (Deauville 1-3 = complete metabolic response). Interim PET-CT after 2-4 cycles is optional and should not change therapy unless it shows progression. Biopsy residual Deauville 4-5 uptake if it would change management. Repeat echocardiogram at end of treatment and during survivorship.
pretreatment_workup: Hepatitis B serology done: HBsAg, anti-HBc and anti-HBs nonreactive, so no HBV reactivation risk from rituximab (consider HBV vaccination). HCV and HIV nonreactive. Echo 2026-09-09: LVEF 45%, GLS -14% (2016: LVEF 62%). Before treatment: cardio-oncology evaluation including ECG, high-sensitivity troponin, NT-proBNP and an ischemic evaluation (coronary CT angiography or stress imaging; left chest radiotherapy raises coronary risk) to define the cause of the LVEF decline; consider cardiac MRI. Bone marrow negative. Creatinine and liver tests normal.
supportive_care: Tumor lysis risk is low-intermediate (LDH ~2.3x ULN, largest mass 7.5 cm, normal creatinine and uric acid): oral hydration and allopurinol starting before cycle 1, with TLS labs at 24-72 hours. Primary G-CSF (pegfilgrastim) with each cycle is reasonable given the febrile neutropenia risk of R-CEOP/R-GCVP and to avoid dose delays. Anastrozole has no meaningful interaction with lymphoma therapy and can continue to complete year 10, or be held during chemotherapy if breast oncology prefers; coordinate with her breast oncologist. Blood pressure (148/90) is controlled with the ACE inhibitor/ARB plus beta-blocker in place of amlodipine. Antiemetics per regimen. Bone health: osteopenia on an aromatase inhibitor plus steroid pulses, continue calcium/vitamin D.
fitness_and_goals: Fit for curative therapy: ECOG 1 (disease-related fatigue and fevers), age 59, normal renal and hepatic function, no heart-failure symptoms (NYHA I). The reduced LVEF changes the regimen, not the curative goal. Her goal is cure and a return to full-time work; explain the trade-off between cardiac safety and the possibly lower efficacy of an anthracycline-free regimen, and decide together with cardio-oncology input. Her worry about her heart (mother with heart failure) is addressed by the cardio-oncology plan and cardioprotection.
